scope: Focused organization, test-discovery/assertion, package, deployment, hosted service and delivery audit. Status answered means the question is resolved from inspected evidence, not necessarily that the behavior is correct. Disputed means a stated or required property conflicts with evidence. Open means a concrete check or design decision remains.

repair_followup.state: Assigned service, delivery, test collection, and test reporting protections repaired with owning checks and in-memory mutants. Original question statuses describe audit-time evidence unless a question explicitly names the repair.

diagnostic_full_suite.limitation: Concurrent working-tree diagnostic. Two failures reported graph module size and classification findings; not a frozen-export qualification.

questions.question: Does serializing and reloading a deny-all endpoint tuple preserve denial?
questions.evidence: Lines 68-72 replace an empty endpoints array with ENDPOINTS; an in-memory roundtrip changed [] to all six endpoints.
questions.discriminating_test: Roundtrip an empty permission set and verify every endpoint remains denied.

questions.question: Can two tenant identities or namespaces alias while using different keys?
questions.evidence: Lines 142-147 check duplicate key digests, but not duplicate tenant identifiers or namespaces.
questions.discriminating_test: Load two distinct keys with repeated tenant identity or namespace; verify an explicit rejection or documented shared-scope decision.

questions.question: Is key comparison performed using constant-time digest comparison?
questions.evidence: Lines 149-156 hash the supplied key and use secrets.compare_digest against stored digests.
questions.discriminating_test: Retain a positive and negative synthetic-key check without recording the keys.

questions.question: Are routes matched to an exact supported version and path?
questions.evidence: Line 160 accepts the last path segment, so any prefix ending in a known endpoint is eligible for dispatch.
questions.discriminating_test: Request /unexpected-prefix/conform and /v999/conform and require the declared routing contract.

questions.question: Are non-object request bodies refused before handler invocation?
questions.evidence: Lines 176-181 reject malformed JSON and a non-dictionary top-level value.
questions.discriminating_test: Supply array, scalar, invalid UTF-8, and malformed JSON bodies and assert the handler is not called.

questions.question: Do unexpected handler errors produce bounded typed responses instead of an abruptly closed connection?
questions.evidence: Lines 185-188 catch ValueError only; KeyError, TypeError, and runtime failures have no response mapping here.
questions.discriminating_test: Inject each non-ValueError exception and verify the chosen protocol error and safe diagnostic.

questions.question: Are malformed, duplicate, and negative Content-Length values refused consistently?
questions.evidence: Lines 211-217 convert Content-Length with int and treat non-positive values as an empty body; no framing error policy appears here.
questions.discriminating_test: Exercise malformed and conflicting headers through an owned local transport fixture.

questions.question: What limits slow body reads, handler duration, and concurrent request threads?
questions.evidence: Lines 212-213 perform a blocking body read; line 240 uses ThreadingHTTPServer without a declared request deadline or thread admission bound.
questions.discriminating_test: Hold a partial request open and flood only a declared local fixture; assert explicit admission and deadline limits.

questions.question: Does metering reject non-finite quantities and times?
questions.evidence: MeteringRecord lines 89-93 check unit membership and quantity < 0, which does not reject NaN or infinity.
questions.discriminating_test: Construct NaN and infinite quantities and timestamps; require refusal before aggregation or JSON serialization.

questions.question: Can the public server inject and restore a durable metering ledger?
questions.evidence: ServiceRequest lines 191-204 has no ledger field, and serve lines 237-240 creates a new in-memory ServiceApplication ledger.
questions.discriminating_test: Restart the service after an acknowledged charge and verify the same durable usage record and total.

questions.question: Does the shipped HTTP service expose provisioning discovery, selection, manifests, and body delivery?
questions.evidence: service_api ENDPOINTS lists health, conform, evaluate, usage, memory_write, and memory_read; default_handlers at service_endpoints:153-155 contains no provisioning adapter.
questions.discriminating_test: Use the installed client against the real transport for one complete qualified material delivery.

questions.question: Does metadata discovery apply tenant-specific disclosure scope?
questions.evidence: ProvisioningServer._offered receives the request but not the authenticated tenant; discover reports total catalog size.
questions.discriminating_test: Create disjoint tenant collections and verify search, withheld identities, item counts, and manifests do not disclose the other collection.

questions.question: Can client-supplied authority_effects be mistaken for host-issued execution authority?
questions.evidence: ProvisioningRequest carries authority_effects and _offered forwards them to offer; no server-issued authority binding appears in this component.
questions.discriminating_test: Forge broader effects in a remote request and verify that server disclosure and later client execution remain bounded by issued authority.

questions.question: Does normal provisioning exclude candidates until independent admission?
questions.evidence: HarnessIntelligenceItem and visibility have kinds, effects, tags, source references and digest, but no authoritative qualification lookup; the prior local review reproduced candidate disclosure.
questions.discriminating_test: Connect source qualification to the normal read path and show that candidate, quarantined, revoked, and unknown records cannot be served as active material.

questions.question: Is the body digest rechecked before a successful read returns?
questions.evidence: ProvisioningServer._read hashes the returned text and refuses mismatches before returning the body.
questions.discriminating_test: Change only the body-reader output and require refusal with no meter call.

questions.question: Is the response size checked against actual encoded bytes at delivery?
questions.evidence: The read response returns item.size_bytes, while _read checks the digest but does not recompute or compare the stored size.
questions.discriminating_test: Register an item with a correct body digest and incorrect size; verify refusal or an explicitly recomputed authoritative size.

questions.question: Does delivery report metered only after an acknowledged charge?
questions.evidence: ProvisioningServer._read returns metered=true even without a callable meter and ignores the callback return value.
questions.discriminating_test: Test absent, failing, false-acknowledgement, unknown, and successful meters separately.

questions.question: Are duplicate provisioning key digests rejected rather than resolved by tuple order?
questions.evidence: ProvisioningServer.tenant_for returns the first matching tenant; this class has no equivalent of ServiceApplication's duplicate-key validation.
questions.discriminating_test: Configure two provisioning tenants with the same digest and require an explicit rejection.

questions.question: Can an item's license, effects, or tags change under the same identity and body digest?
questions.evidence: HarnessIntelligenceCatalogue.register at harness_intelligence:158-166 only refuses a changed body digest, then replaces the whole item.
questions.discriminating_test: Re-register one identity with unchanged bytes but widened effects or changed qualification-relevant metadata; require a new version or exact refusal.

questions.question: Does public solve dependency construction install the catalog needed by the Spawned Loop provisioning hook?
questions.evidence: solve_runtime:537-546 installs capability_directory and intelligence_catalog but not harness_catalogue or guardrails; spawned_provisioning returns no_catalogue_installed.
questions.discriminating_test: Start at solve_task and inspect actual offered material and written assignment files for a spawned assignment.

questions.question: Does a manifest file digest mismatch prevent any candidate code from executing?
questions.evidence: verify_export:347-360 records the mismatch, then still calls _run_isolated; the safe probe observed one execution callback after the failed digest check.
questions.discriminating_test: Mutate one file and assert no interpreter, tests, or entry point starts.

questions.question: Is the supplied manifest_digest recomputed and checked?
questions.evidence: verify_export returns the manifest_digest at line 380 without recomputing it; the safe probe returned a forged value.
questions.discriminating_test: Change only manifest content or manifest_digest and require refusal before execution.

questions.question: Are manifest-listed paths confined and symlink-checked again during verification?
questions.evidence: verify_export joins arbitrary manifest files keys onto root at lines 347-355, unlike ExportedFile's path validation.
questions.discriminating_test: Use synthetic absolute, traversal, and symlink paths in an otherwise valid manifest and assert no outside read.

questions.question: Is package_name from a loaded manifest validated before insertion into interpreter source?
questions.evidence: verify_export:345 and 359 interpolate the raw string; the package-name regex is enforced on SolutionExportSpec, not the loaded manifest.
questions.discriminating_test: Load a malformed manifest package name and verify refusal before composing or running interpreter code.

questions.question: Are loaded isolation values restricted to the declared modes?
questions.evidence: _isolated_python selects -I/-S for stdlib_only and -I for every other value; verify_export reads the manifest value without enum validation.
questions.discriminating_test: Supply an unknown isolation value and require a typed refusal.

questions.question: Which declared sandbox and effect authority govern exported candidate code during verification?
questions.evidence: _run_isolated:321-323 invokes a local subprocess with Python import-isolation flags and a reduced environment; it does not invoke the workspace sandbox boundary.
questions.discriminating_test: Run a controlled candidate that attempts an undeclared file or network effect inside the intended sandbox and verify refusal.

questions.question: Can an export with no test directory be labeled passed after only import checks?
questions.evidence: verify_export:363 conditionally omits test execution when tests/ is absent; tests default to an empty tuple in SolutionExportSpec.
questions.discriminating_test: Assert that the report names import-only verification and cannot be promoted as independently task-qualified.

questions.question: Does the export specification digest bind container resources and invocation arguments?
questions.evidence: SolutionExportSpec.digest:157-164 omits container, isolation and python_requires; the safe probe changed resources and arguments without changing the digest.
questions.discriminating_test: Change each behavior-affecting field separately and require identity changes under the declared digest contract.

questions.question: Do generic exported resources survive packaging, including nested templates and text files?
questions.evidence: ExportedFile accepts text files generally, while render_pyproject:183 includes only *.json and *.yaml package data.
questions.discriminating_test: Export a package using a nested HTML template, build and install the wheel, and read it outside the source tree.

questions.question: Does standalone verification exercise an installed distribution rather than adding src to the interpreter path?
questions.evidence: verify_export:359 and 365 insert src into sys.path; no wheel build or installation occurs in this path.
questions.discriminating_test: Build and install the exact export in a fresh environment, then run its public entry point with fresh inputs.

questions.question: Are installed architecture and terminology projections checked for equality with repository authorities?
questions.evidence: architecture_contract chooses root YAML when present and packaged YAML otherwise; this review did not execute a projection equality check.
questions.discriminating_test: Compare both authority pairs at the exact export tree and run the same invariant checks from an installed wheel.

questions.question: Is every shipped non-Python resource classified as runtime data rather than accepted through broad wildcards?
questions.evidence: pyproject.toml includes recursive Markdown, HTML, JSON, JSONL, and YAML patterns.
questions.discriminating_test: Compare wheel data files against a reviewed runtime resource manifest and refuse unexpected records.

questions.question: Are local run and Studio state paths excluded from distribution?
questions.evidence: pyproject.toml exclude-package-data covers evidence/runs and evidence/studio; CI inspects the built wheel for these paths.
questions.discriminating_test: Retain canaries for each excluded path in a disposable build export and check both wheel and source distribution.

questions.question: Does the optional-backend import check actually make installed optional providers unavailable?
questions.evidence: backend_isolation.base_import_report only removes selected sys.modules entries; imports may reload installed providers and cached base modules may bypass import work.
questions.discriminating_test: Use a fresh subprocess with an import blocker or a genuinely minimal environment, and plant a forbidden import.

questions.question: Are production and build dependencies locked sufficiently to reproduce a published image?
questions.evidence: pyproject.toml leaves several dependencies unpinned; Dockerfile upgrades pip and installs the project without a lock file.
questions.discriminating_test: Rebuild the same source with a frozen dependency set and compare manifests; state which differences are intentionally allowed.

questions.question: Can two releases be distinguished beyond the unchanged Python distribution version?
questions.evidence: pyproject.toml reports 0.1.0 while the image workflow also adds commit labels; installed package provenance is not equivalent to the image label.
questions.discriminating_test: Produce a source-and-dependency build identity in the installed distribution and compare two source revisions.

questions.question: Do all names in the lazy public facade resolve in supported installation variants?
questions.evidence: __init__.py maps public names to string module/attribute pairs and imports them lazily; no complete facade resolution run was performed here.
questions.discriminating_test: Resolve the declared public surface in base and selected-extra installations while blocking accidental effects.

questions.question: Are console-script and Python-requirement values safely serialized into generated project metadata?
questions.evidence: render_pyproject interpolates console_script and python_requires directly; SolutionExportSpec validates names and version but not these fields.
questions.discriminating_test: Supply quotes, newlines, invalid entry-point names, and invalid version requirements and require typed validation or safe serialization.

questions.question: Does a failed pip installation fail the Docker image build?
questions.evidence: Dockerfile:20-22 ends the entire && chain with || true; a harmless equivalent shell chain returned success after false.
questions.discriminating_test: Make the install command fail in an isolated build fixture and require a nonzero build result.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Can a public image tag be updated before source tests and image acceptance have passed?
questions.evidence: publish-image.yml runs independently on push, publishes in Build and push, then executes doctor.
questions.discriminating_test: Build once, qualify the exact digest, and publish/promote only after the required checks for that revision succeed.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does the image smoke test establish service or solve behavior?
questions.evidence: publish-image.yml only runs doctor and checks for a nonempty dictionary; cli_operations.run_doctor explicitly checks configuration, not provider or sandbox operation.
questions.discriminating_test: Add offline installed-image service and client acceptance matched to the release claim.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does publication retain a build provenance attestation?
questions.evidence: publish-image.yml Build and push sets provenance: false despite attaching source revision labels.
questions.discriminating_test: Verify signed or otherwise governed source/build provenance for the exact published digest.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does the recipe checker reject numeric root user declarations?
questions.evidence: examples/28 run.py rejects only the literal USER root; a USER 0 fixture passed every Dockerfile check.
questions.discriminating_test: Require refusal of USER 0, 0:0, and equivalent root declarations.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does the recipe checker validate the syntax of a base-image digest?
questions.evidence: Its check only looks for @sha256:; the safe fixture sha256:invalid passed.
questions.discriminating_test: Require exactly the supported digest algorithm and hex length and then verify resolution in a build check.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does removing the base-image digest fail the example's overall status?
questions.evidence: examples/28 run.py marks base_image_digest_pinned as non-required in main; the README calls it a warning.
questions.discriminating_test: Remove the digest and assert the production qualification gate fails, while retaining any explicitly separate development mode.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does following the example deployment guide configure the authenticated readiness header?
questions.evidence: worker-deployment.yaml uses READINESS_KEY_FROM_SECRET as a literal header, while the README only instructs replacing IMAGE_REFERENCE and creating the tenants Secret.
questions.discriminating_test: Render the actual deployment configuration and show readiness authenticates without exposing a key in published manifests.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: What state survives a worker replacement or replica increase?
questions.evidence: worker-deployment.yaml mounts /work from emptyDir and the default service stores are in memory.
questions.discriminating_test: Replace the worker and exercise two replicas; verify the selected durable store's tenant, usage, and record consistency.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Can the non-root image write every declared output location and shut down cleanly?
questions.evidence: Dockerfile switches to user 65534 and /work; no actual image filesystem/cancellation test was run in this audit.
questions.discriminating_test: Run an owned exact-image smoke test against mounted work storage and verify output ownership, termination, and cleanup.
questions.owning_boundary: Dockerfile, publication workflow, and worker deployment

questions.question: Does test collection detect a self_test moved into a nested package?
questions.evidence: _conformance_scan:676 skips paths deeper than two segments; the in-memory nested-file fixture produced no findings.
questions.discriminating_test: Move a test module one level deeper without registering it and require the collection gate to fail.

questions.question: Are all root modules exempt from collection checks even when their self_test is not called?
questions.evidence: _conformance_scan:678-681 skips every name in ROOT_MODULES.
questions.discriminating_test: Remove one root self-test from the actual suite and require an uncollected-test failure.

questions.question: Can an unrelated quoted module name make the collection detector believe a suite is registered?
questions.evidence: Collection uses regex over source text at _conformance_scan:667-671; an unrelated string fixture produced no findings.
questions.discriminating_test: Mention an unregistered module only in a comment or string and require the detector to report it.

questions.question: Does the aggregator reject an empty module test report?
questions.evidence: _fold accepts tests=[]; mocking every module report empty produced passed=1, total=1, all_passed=true.
questions.discriminating_test: Require nonempty checks or a separately typed, justified unavailable outcome per collected module.

questions.question: Are folded module identities unique?
questions.evidence: The actual list has 385 entries and 381 distinct module names; four ontology modules occur twice.
questions.discriminating_test: Reject duplicate module registration and distinguish invocation count from unique behavior checks.

questions.question: Are optional adapters counted separately from passed behavioral checks?
questions.evidence: Missing optional adapters return passed=true with not_tested=true and contribute to the aggregate passed count.
questions.discriminating_test: Report executed passes, failures, unavailable checks, and denominator separately; assert summary consistency.

questions.question: Does one crashing module produce a failed record while allowing other suites to run?
questions.evidence: _fold catches exceptions and returns a failed record; the aggregator carries a timeout-fixture assertion.
questions.discriminating_test: Keep an exception fixture and verify it cannot become a passed or skipped result.

questions.question: Are individual result records required to carry actual Boolean passed values?
questions.evidence: The aggregator sums truthy r[passed] values without validating every record shape or Boolean type.
questions.discriminating_test: Return passed='false', missing passed, a non-list tests value, and duplicate identities; require typed aggregate failures.

questions.question: Are check identities unique and stable enough to compare coverage across releases?
questions.evidence: Modules emit either test or name keys; the aggregator concatenates records and does not enforce unique qualified identities.
questions.discriminating_test: Compare exact check identities across exports and flag removed or duplicated checks independently of total count.

questions.question: Does the service self-test shut down its owned listener and thread?
questions.evidence: service_api.self_test:308-334 starts serve in a daemon thread, tests health, and returns without stopping the server or joining the thread.
questions.discriminating_test: Invoke the suite repeatedly in one process and assert there are no remaining owned listeners or threads.

questions.question: Does the dependency-direction detector catch ordinary absolute import statements?
questions.evidence: scan_dependency_direction examines ast.ImportFrom only; the equivalent ast.Import fixture produced zero findings.
questions.discriminating_test: Require the same result for import, from-import, and aliased forms of the same dependency.

questions.question: Will relative dependency detection remain correct after adding another package level?
questions.evidence: The detector recognizes relative imports only when node.level == 2 and uses the first source path segment.
questions.discriminating_test: Move a fixture into core/family and test every valid relative spelling against resolved module identity.

questions.question: Does current conformance distinguish tolerated dependency debt from a clean boundary?
questions.evidence: The read-only scan found 73 dependency_direction findings against a baseline of 73; clean=false, while the separate architecture contract passed.
questions.discriminating_test: Preserve the 73-debt count in public status instead of reducing all evidence to one pass flag.

questions.question: Can replacing one existing bad dependency with a new bad dependency pass a count-only ratchet?
questions.evidence: The ratchet compares aggregate counts with a ceiling; it does not bind the existing exact edge set.
questions.discriminating_test: Remove one baseline edge and add an unrelated forbidden edge, then decide whether the policy should reject the new edge.

questions.question: Are cached source trees invalidated when files change in a long-lived process?
questions.evidence: _source_text, _source_tree, and _py_files_cached have unbounded path-only caches with no file identity input.
questions.discriminating_test: Scan, change a fixture, and scan again in the same process; require the second result to reflect new bytes.

questions.question: Does the boundary register match exact module identities rather than substrings?
questions.evidence: scan_unregistered_boundaries uses if mod in registered, where registered is one joined string.
questions.discriminating_test: Use two module names where one is a substring of the other and require distinct registration decisions.

questions.question: Can an envelope call through an alias or attribute bypass unregistered-boundary discovery?
questions.evidence: The scanner collects only direct ast.Name calls with six exact spellings.
questions.discriminating_test: Call the same envelope via an imported alias and a module attribute; require equivalent detection.

questions.question: Do repository and bootstrap import guards use the same forbidden development roots?
questions.evidence: repository_conformance omits loop_engine_devtools from its forbidden roots, while the independent bootstrap includes it.
questions.discriminating_test: Run the same forbidden import fixtures through both guards and document intentional scope differences.

questions.question: Does a code_ref validate the named symbol as well as importing its module?
questions.evidence: repository_conformance.reference_violations drops the final dotted segment and only imports the resulting module.
questions.discriminating_test: Reference a nonexistent symbol in an existing module and require reference-integrity failure.

questions.question: Does the repository Node-class detector cover classes nested in functions and classes?
questions.evidence: repository_conformance.node_class_violations inspects tree.body only; other invariants may cover a subset separately.
questions.discriminating_test: Plant a uniquely named nested forbidden class and verify that the actual required gate reports it.

questions.question: Does the physical core directory provide useful ownership boundaries at its current size?
questions.evidence: The current directory contains 362 Python files directly; the September 18 folder-depth record describes a proposed migration rather than a completed move.
questions.discriminating_test: Choose one existing boundary by dependency isolation and verify a move without changing behavior or public imports.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Are README-only package folders being mistaken for implemented package separation?
questions.evidence: The layout record says six declared areas hold contracts/data while behavior resides in core, catalog, memory, and strings.
questions.discriminating_test: Label conceptual boundaries and physical implementation ownership separately in the architecture view.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: How much cross-module private-symbol coupling exists, and how much is test-only?
questions.evidence: An AST census found 131 private import statements and 266 imported private symbols; a heuristic excluding named check modules/functions left 75 statements and 149 symbols.
questions.discriminating_test: Classify each remaining edge as deliberate shared boundary, compatibility dependency, test helper, or refactor candidate before renaming files.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Which private source-reading helpers should have a stable owning interface?
questions.evidence: task_materials:32-34 imports _open_source and private source classification constants from adaptive_practitioner_source.
questions.discriminating_test: Change the source-admission implementation behind a stable contract and rerun archive and ordinary-source refusal checks.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Can a static import closure be read as proof of actual public-path invocation?
questions.evidence: reachability_report uses ast.walk including self_test bodies; the current report says 350/587 reachable while public provisioning dependencies are absent.
questions.discriminating_test: Require an observed public-boundary call and result record independently from static import reachability.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Does static non-reachability prove a module is unused when dispatch uses strings?
questions.evidence: reachability_report itself excludes the string-driven public facade from analysis, but its docstring describes dark modules as dark under any reading.
questions.discriminating_test: Compare static misses against known lazy facade and registry dispatches before calling any module unused.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Is the public solve capability inventory broad enough to represent first-release integration?
questions.evidence: REQUIRED_REACHABLE contains eight selected modules and does not assert provisioning transport, qualification, durable metering, or client material loading.
questions.discriminating_test: Build an acceptance inventory from requested behaviors, each with public-path observation and refusal checks.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Are generated architecture findings computed from current source rather than embedded narrative?
questions.evidence: tools/export_component_inventory.py emits several fixed findings and states, including context-handoff status, alongside computed inventory.
questions.discriminating_test: Bind each narrative finding to a current check or explicitly mark it historical or proposed.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Are integration package checks executed by continuous integration?
questions.evidence: No reference to integrations/tests/check_integrations.py was found in the inspected CI/test entry points; it passed locally with four manifests and six skills.
questions.discriminating_test: Add or identify the owning CI job and plant an invalid integration manifest to prove the job fails.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Are the thirteen host-runtime example test files executed by continuous integration?
questions.evidence: The inspected CI workflow does not discover examples/25_host_runtime or run example 25; the selected resource-catalog file contains substantive refusal and process-parity tests.
questions.discriminating_test: Collect these suites under an explicit offline/live partition and prove each intended offline check is executed.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Does base-wheel acceptance exercise the full installed self-test and all first-release behavior?
questions.evidence: CI default-install block runs pip check, doctor, setup, Studio self-test, and CLI acceptance; it does not run the full installed self-test or provisioning transport acceptance.
questions.discriminating_test: Run the exact claimed base-install public paths outside the source tree, with unsupported extras reported separately.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Does the generic registered api endpoint actually cover the newly added hosted service path?
questions.evidence: boundary_registry:154-158 binds api endpoint to core.saas_routes.serve_api; ServiceApplication dispatches its own handlers.
questions.discriminating_test: Trace a real hosted request to an exact registered owning Loop and verify that every new operational boundary has its own truthful registration.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Do solver identifiers distinguish different executable specifications and catalogs?
questions.evidence: service_endpoints:34 identifies recorded solvers only by output count; line 60 identifies text conformance by two thresholds.
questions.discriminating_test: Change rules, catalogs, or recorded outputs while holding their counts/thresholds fixed and require distinguishable implementation identities.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Do frozen record types also freeze mutable nested mappings?
questions.evidence: EvaluationCase is frozen but retains input, expected, and grader_parameters objects; HarnessIntelligenceCatalogue exposes its mutable items dictionary.
questions.discriminating_test: Mutate nested data after admission and verify immutable identity, rejection, or a new version rather than silent behavior drift.
questions.owning_boundary: existing owning component named by evidence

questions.question: Can a remote evaluation request choose its own physical catalog root, and does the repair preserve legitimate local and tenant-scoped catalog use?
questions.evidence: The audit reproduced caller-selected catalog reads through real service dispatch with only the final read intercepted. The authorized repair adds ServiceCatalogScope, rejects request catalog_root, selects scope by authenticated tenant, denies file catalogs by default, and preserves local solver file specifications. Endpoint suite 8/8 and catalog authority mutants passed their discriminating checks.
questions.discriminating_test: Remove root rejection, tenant binding, reference validation, or configured catalog loading independently. Require the existing endpoint checks to reject each mutant while a valid scoped catalog changes the observed output.
